title: Problem Overview: 3-Fold Convolution Linear Error
content: Erdos Problem #764 asks: can the 3-fold convolution sum sum_{n<=N} 1_A * 1_A * 1_A(n) equal cN + O(1) for some A subset N and c > 0? The answer is NO, proved by Vaughan (1972). Even the weaker bound cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}) is impossible. This generalizes the Erdos-Fuchs theorem (1956) for 2-fold convolutions (Problem #763) and applies to any h-fold convolution with h >= 2.
mathContext: $\sum_{n \leq N} (1_A * 1_A * 1_A)(n) = cN + O(1)$? Answer: NO. Even $cN + o(N^{1/4}/(\log N)^{1/2})$ is impossible (Vaughan 1972). Here $(1_A^{*h})(n) = \#\{(a_1, \ldots, a_h) \in A^h : a_1 + \cdots + a_h = n\}$.

title: Convolution Counting Functions
content: charFun A n is the characteristic function (1 if n in A, 0 otherwise). conv2 A n counts pairs (a,b) in A x A with a+b=n, implemented via Finset.filter on Finset.product of Finset.range(n+1). conv3 A n counts triples (a,b,c) in A^3 with a+b+c=n, using a triple product. convH h A n (axiom) is the general h-fold convolution, axiomatized because a clean definition requires dependent types. sumConv2 and sumConv3 are cumulative sums over [0,N].
mathContext: $\text{conv2}(A, n) = |\{(a,b) \in A^2 : a+b=n\}|$ via `Finset.filter` on `Finset.product (Finset.range (n+1)) (Finset.range (n+1))`. $\text{conv3}(A, n) = |\{(a,b,c) \in A^3 : a+b+c=n\}|$ via triple product. $\text{sumConv3}(A, N) = \sum_{n=0}^{N} \text{conv3}(A, n) = r_3(N)$, the cumulative representation count.

title: Error Bound Hierarchy
content: Three levels of approximation quality. IsLinearBounded f c: f(N) = cN + O(1), meaning |f(N) - cN| <= M for some fixed M. This is what Erdos asked about. IsLinearLittleO f c alpha: f(N) = cN + o(N^alpha), the error grows slower than N^alpha. IsLinearVaughan f c: f(N) = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}), the precise bound Vaughan proved impossible. The hierarchy: IsLinearBounded implies IsLinearVaughan implies IsLinearLittleO (for alpha = 1/4).
mathContext: $\text{IsLinearBounded}(f, c) := \exists M, \forall N, |f(N) - cN| \leq M$. $\text{IsLinearLittleO}(f, c, \alpha) := \forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists N_0, \forall N \geq N_0, |f(N) - cN| < \varepsilon N^\alpha$. $\text{IsLinearVaughan}(f, c) := \forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists N_0, \forall N \geq N_0, |f(N) - cN| < \varepsilon \frac{N^{1/4}}{\sqrt{\log N}}$. Implications: $O(1) \subset o(N^{1/4}/\sqrt{\log N}) \subset o(N^{1/4})$.

title: Erdos-Fuchs Theorem (2-Fold Case, 1956)
content: erdos_fuchs_theorem (axiom): no set A has sum 1_A * 1_A = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}). This is the foundational 1956 result establishing that representation functions must fluctuate. erdos_fuchs_corollary (axiom): no set A has sum 1_A * 1_A = cN + O(1). Follows because bounded error is a special case of the Vaughan error bound. These establish the 2-fold baseline that Problem #764 generalizes.
mathContext: `erdos_fuchs_theorem : \forall A, c > 0, \neg\text{IsLinearVaughan}(\text{sumConv2}(A), c)$. `erdos_fuchs_corollary : \forall A, c > 0, \neg\text{IsLinearBounded}(\text{sumConv2}(A), c)$. The original proof uses exponential sums and Parseval's identity: $\sum |\hat{f}|^2 = \sum |f|^2$.

title: Vaughan's Theorem: 3-Fold and h-Fold Impossibility
content: vaughan_3fold_theorem (axiom): no set A has sum 1_A * 1_A * 1_A = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}). The strong form proving even this weak error bound is impossible. vaughan_corollary (axiom): no set A has sum 1_A * 1_A * 1_A = cN + O(1). This is the direct answer to Erdos Problem #764: NO. vaughan_hfold_theorem (axiom): for any h >= 2, the h-fold convolution sum cannot be cN + O(1). Vaughan's proof technique extends the Erdos-Fuchs exponential sum method to higher-order convolutions.
mathContext:
`vaughan_3fold_theorem :  orall A, c > 0, 
eg	ext{IsLinearVaughan}(	ext{sumConv3}(A), c)$. `vaughan_corollary :  orall A, c > 0, 
eg	ext{IsLinearBounded}(	ext{sumConv3}(A), c)$. `vaughan_hfold_theorem :  orall h \geq 2,  orall A, c > 0, 
eg	ext{IsLinearBounded}(\sum_{n \leq N} 	ext{convH}(h, A, n), c)$.

title: Error Oscillation: Both Sides of Zero
content: ErrorOscillates f c: the error f(N) - cN is infinitely often above N^{1/4} and infinitely often below -N^{1/4}. The error cannot stay bounded on one side — it must cross zero infinitely many times with amplitude at least N^{1/4}. error_oscillation (axiom): for any infinite set A and c > 0, the 3-fold convolution error oscillates. This strengthens Vaughan's impossibility by showing the error is not merely unbounded but must change sign.
mathContext: $\text{ErrorOscillates}(f, c) := (\forall N_0, \exists N \geq N_0, f(N) - cN > N^{1/4}) \wedge (\forall N_0, \exists N \geq N_0, f(N) - cN < -N^{1/4})$. `error_oscillation : A.\text{Infinite} \Rightarrow \text{ErrorOscillates}(\text{sumConv3}(A), c)$. The oscillation is not symmetric in general.

title: Squares Example: Proved Application
content: squares_not_linear (PROVED): even for A = {0, 1, 4, 9, 16, ...} (perfect squares), the 3-fold convolution sum cannot be cN + O(1). Proved directly by applying vaughan_corollary to Squares. This connects to Waring's problem: the number of representations of n as a sum of 3 squares is known to be ~(pi/4) * n^{1/2} * S(n) where S is a singular series, far from linear growth.
mathContext: `squares_not_linear : \forall c > 0, \neg\text{IsLinearBounded}(\text{sumConv3}(\text{Squares}), c)$. Proved: `vaughan_corollary Squares c hc`. The 3-square representation count $r_3(n)$ has fluctuations governed by class numbers.

title: Montgomery-Vaughan Refinement and Tightness
content: montgomery_vaughan_refinement (axiom): even o(N^{1/4}) is impossible for 2-fold convolutions, removing the logarithmic factor from Erdos-Fuchs. quarter_exponent_tight (axiom): there exist sets where the error is O(N^alpha) for any alpha > 1/4. Together these show the 1/4 exponent is exactly the critical threshold — it cannot be improved to any smaller exponent, but the log factor can be removed.
mathContext: `montgomery_vaughan_refinement : \forall A, c > 0, \neg\text{IsLinearLittleO}(\text{sumConv2}(A), c, 1/4)$. `quarter_exponent_tight : \exists A, c > 0, \forall \alpha > 1/4, \text{IsLinearLittleO}(\text{sumConv2}(A), c, \alpha)$. The critical exponent $1/4$ matches the Fourier-analytic prediction from $L^2$ norms.
